name: 10128-sharedprefix-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1. An 8B model fits one 80GB card.
architecture: Dense decoder (LlamaForCausalLM), 32 layers, 32 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, max_position_embeddings 8192, bf16, 8.03B params.
load_profile: poisson (OPEN loop), rate 112 req/s scored, with 200 req/s (deliberately oversubscribed, so the achieved rate reads the sustained ceiling directly) and 128 req/s as the other two rungs; each bounded at 5600 requests / 900 s safety, warmup the first 10% by requests. 10 req/s is the rate the objective was written against, on a card several times slower than this one; on this H100 the same engine sustains 94.1 req/s MEASURED 2026-08-22, so 10 req/s leaves it at 11% load and nothing queues. The scored rate holds the objective's own ratio of offered rate to sustained rate (10/9.02 = 1.109) against the sustained rate measured HERE; guidellm delivers ~95.5% of a declared rate, so a declared 112 is an arrival rate of ~107 and an offered/sustained ratio of 1.137. The request COUNT is then derived so that the ARRIVAL WINDOW matches the objective's own ~50 s (5600 / 112 = 50.0 s, against the objective's 500 / 10 = 50.0 s), because the mean wait under an oversubscribed open loop is proportional to that window in seconds while the per-request floor is set by step latency, which this card does not shorten by anything like the same factor. Holding the count at 500 instead would compress the window to 4.5 s -- comparable to the 1.5 s it takes the generation pipeline to fill -- and read a ramp rather than a stream. An open-loop rate is not enforced by default in this harness.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, ONE prefix bucket (bucket_weight 100, prefix_count 1, prefix_tokens 600); prompt EXACTLY 200 tokens and output EXACTLY 30, so every request is 600 shared + 200 unique = 800 prompt tokens. `request_format: plain` is required rather than stylistic: the templated path reads `engine.tokenizer`, which this era's `AsyncLLMEngine` does not expose.
purpose: An 8B support assistant answering brief questions behind a shared instruction prefix at 110 requests per second on one GPU.
launch:
# Ungated mirror of the gated meta-llama repo, same weights.
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct

enable-prefix-caching: true

# Not on by default at this version; it has to be asked for.
enable-chunked-prefill: true

max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
max-num-seqs: 256

# This era raises if max_num_batched_tokens % block_size != 0; 2048 % 16 = 0.
block-size: 16

tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Every request otherwise logs its full 800-token prompt repr. It applies to every run: it is
# instrument overhead, not an engine setting, and the objective's own command disables it.
disable-log-requests: true
